look_here_first: Start with the leaves and flower spikes. Hall's prairie clover is a slender perennial with mostly 3-foliolate leaves, sparse wiry stems, and relatively loose spikes of conspicuous yellow flowers. The calyx ribs/teeth are often reddish-brown and hairy.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx ribs and teeth often red/chestnut-brown

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calcareous prairie and rocky limestone habitat

lookalikes.differences: Unlike purple-flowered D. purpurea, D. hallii has yellow flowers and typically 3-foliolate leaves. Unlike D. candida, the spikes are looser and flowers yellow rather than white.
